questions.stem: This action potential shows markedly prolonged repolarization due to potassium-current blockade, greatly increasing the action potential duration and effective refractory period with little change in phase 0. Which agent is the prototype for this effect?

explanation.summary: Selective prolongation of repolarization via K+ channel block (increased APD and ERP) defines Class III antiarrhythmics, prototypically amiodarone, sotalol, dofetilide, and ibutilide. Lidocaine is IB, flecainide IC, verapamil IV.
explanation.whyCorrect: Selective prolongation of repolarization via K+ channel block (increased APD and ERP) defines Class III antiarrhythmics, prototypically amiodarone, sotalol, dofetilide, and ibutilide. Lidocaine is IB, flecainide IC, verapamil IV.

questions.stem: This pacemaker (nodal) action potential shows a drug decreasing the slope of phase 4 spontaneous depolarization and prolonging repolarization at the AV node. Which agent produces this effect?

explanation.summary: Reducing the slope of phase 4 depolarization in pacemaker cells (slowing SA-node firing and AV-node conduction) is the mechanism of Class II beta blockers such as metoprolol and propranolol. They decrease heart rate and prolong AV nodal refractoriness by blunting sympathetic (cAMP) drive.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reducing the slope of phase 4 depolarization in pacemaker cells (slowing SA-node firing and AV-node conduction) is the mechanism of Class II beta blockers such as metoprolol and propranolol. They decrease heart rate and prolong AV nodal refractoriness by blunting sympathetic (cAMP) drive.

questions.stem: This action potential (dark curve) shows a slow upstroke and prolonged repolarization at the AV node compared with a normal fast-response cell. Which ionic mechanism is chiefly responsible for the slowed upstroke seen here?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rapid Na+ influx through fast sodium channels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Depolarization depends on slow inward Ca2+ current

explanation.summary: AV nodal (slow-response) cells depend on the slow inward Ca2+ current for their upstroke. Class IV agents (non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers) blunt this current, slowing the rise and prolonging AV nodal conduction/repolarization.
explanation.whyCorrect: AV nodal (slow-response) cells depend on the slow inward Ca2+ current for their upstroke. Class IV agents (non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers) blunt this current, slowing the rise and prolonging AV nodal conduction/repolarization.
